slides.0.title: Wachau
slides.0.subtitle: Terraces and the three Vinea Wachau grades
slides.1.title: Regional profile
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Scale
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About 1,324 ha (2022 data) along a narrow Danube valley with steep terraces
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Soils
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Upper terraces are Gföhl gneiss, amphibolite and quartzite; lower slopes are loess, sand and gravel. Riesling tends to sit on gneiss and Grüner Veltliner on loess
slides.1.highlights.2.title: DAC timing
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Wachau DAC became compulsory from the 2020 vintage, was approved in August 2021 and is the 15th DAC
slides.1.content: Wachau is small, yet among the most famous and priciest names in Austria.
slides.2.title: The three Vinea Wachau grades
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Steinfeder
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Federspiel
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Medium body, 11.5–12.5% abv, residual sugar no more than 4 g/L
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Smaragd
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The richest, at least 12.5% abv and 18.5 °KMW, released no earlier than 1 May after the harvest
slides.2.highlights.3.title: The Vinea Wachau association
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Founded in 1983; the three grades are its trademarks (since 1984), with over 200 members controlling about 85% of the land
slides.2.content: The three grades are separated by alcohol and ripeness.
slides.3.title: Wachau DAC's geographic tiers
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Gebietswein
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Ortswein
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Village level, limited to 9 white varieties
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Riedenwein
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Single-vineyard level, only Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, from 157 Rieden
slides.3.content: The Vinea Wachau grades can still be used alongside; DAC adds a statutory geographic framework.
Which Wachau grade is the richest, released no earlier than 1 May after harvest?
Smaragd is at least 12.5% abv and not released before 1 May of the following year.
What is the residual sugar limit for Federspiel?
Federspiel is 11.5–12.5% abv with no more than 4 g/L residual sugar.
Which two varieties are allowed for Wachau DAC Riedenwein?
Riedenwein is limited to Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
